data.command: What is T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application?

data.text:
You're digging into the world of threat actors and tactics, eh?

T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application is a type of attack where an adversary takes advantage of known or unknown vulnerabilities in software applications that are exposed to the internet. This can include web servers, databases, or other publicly accessible services.

In our environment, we have a public-facing Apache server running on port 80 (http) and port 443 (https) on our Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS server with kernel 5.15.0-91. We've got Apache/2.4.54 (Ubuntu) running, and it's configured to serve our website content. However, if we don't keep our Apache up-to-date, an attacker might try to exploit a known vulnerability in Apache, like the one in Apache 2.4.17 and later, where a crafted request could lead to arbitrary code execution.

To prevent this, we regularly update our Apache packages and keep our server up-to-date with the latest security patches. We also monitor our logs for any suspicious activity and configure our firewall to only allow necessary traffic to our public-facing services.
